カップ.intro: Cups (the Holy Grail) correspond to the element of water and govern emotion, relationships, love, and heartfelt satisfaction. The numbered cards from Ace to Ten trace a flow in which feelings overflow, are shared with someone, pass through disappointment and uncertainty, and move toward deep fulfillment. The court cards show what kind of person you are in how you use sensitivity and empathy. When Cups appear as you face a decision, they offer a chance to turn your attention to what conditions and logic alone make hard to see — “How do I really feel?” and “What will happen to my relationships with the people who matter to me?” They are a suit you can rely on when organizing a decision you're torn over, where your head has decided but your heart hasn't caught up. Smaller numbers tend to show the first stirrings of feeling, while larger numbers show mature satisfaction and the completion of a relationship. Try reading them while checking which stage your own heart is at right now.
カップ.label: Cups

ソード.intro: Swords correspond to the element of air and govern thought, judgment, words, and conflict. The numbered cards from Ace to Ten depict a clear insight at the start, then uncertainty, heartache, maneuvering, anxiety, and finally a break and a fresh start — and many of the images are stark. The court cards show what kind of person you are in how you use intellect and words. When Swords appear as you face a decision, they are useful as a viewpoint for checking, “Am I separating facts from assumptions?” and “Is fear clouding my judgment?” This is a suit that is especially powerful for choices where you need to face a difficult situation directly, sharpen your thinking, and draw a line. Even a stark image can be read as a sign that says, “Here is a risk to notice — and a chance to think again.” Try reflecting on which stage your thinking is at within the flow of the numbers.
ソード.label: Swords

ペンタクル.intro: Pentacles (coins) correspond to the element of earth and govern money, work, skill, health, and the foundations of daily life. The numbered cards from Ace to Ten trace a steady flow: you seize a small opportunity, build through ingenuity and effort, gain savings and results, and pass them on to the next generation. The court cards show what kind of person you are in how you cultivate and use practical strength. When Pentacles appear as you face a decision, they are useful as a viewpoint for checking, “Do I have a clear outlook on time and money?” and “Is this shaped in a way I can sustain over the long term?” They are especially helpful for choices directly tied to daily life, such as changing jobs, moving house, or making a purchase. Smaller numbers tend to show the seed-planting stage, while larger numbers show the stage of harvest and inheritance. Many of these cards remind you of the value of building steadily, without rushing.
ペンタクル.label: Pentacles

ワンド.intro: Wands correspond to the element of fire and govern passion, motivation, action, and challenge. The numbered cards from Ace to Ten trace a flow: an idea sparks, a plan takes shape, you compete, you achieve results, and eventually you take on a heavy load. The court cards — Page, Knight, Queen, and King — show what kind of person you are in how you handle that energy. When Wands appear as you face a decision, they are useful as a viewpoint for checking, “Which option do I truly want to pursue?” and “Is the balance between momentum and preparation right?” They are especially helpful for choices where your feelings may run ahead of you, or when you stand before a new challenge. Even within Wands, smaller numbers tend to show the momentum of beginnings, while larger numbers show the responsibility you have taken on. Try reading them while reflecting on which stage your own enthusiasm is at right now.
ワンド.label: Wands

大アルカナ.intro: The Major Arcana are the 22 cards from The Fool to The World, forming the backbone of the tarot's story. Each one depicts, as a symbol, a stage in life's larger flow — setting out, learning, trials, loss, renewal, and completion. More than everyday events, they tend to reflect questions about your values and the direction of your life itself. When a Major Arcana card appears as you face a decision, it can be a prompt to think beyond the immediate pros and cons and ask, “Does this choice connect to the kind of person I want to be?” Read in numerical order, the cards link together as a single story of growth, and the meanings of the cards before and after each one come into view. Card 0, The Fool, is the figure who steps forward carrying nothing, and the remaining 21 cards are easier to remember if you think of them as the people, events, and states of mind encountered on that journey. The deeper the decision you're torn over, the more it helps to look not just at a single card's meaning, but at its place within the flow.
大アルカナ.label: Major Arcana

indexFaq.a: There are 78. They consist of the 22 Major Arcana, which represent life's larger flow and themes, and the 56 Minor Arcana (four suits — Wands, Cups, Swords, and Pentacles — of 14 cards each), which represent everyday events and feelings. On this page, all 78 cards are explained one by one.
indexFaq.q: How many tarot cards are there in total?

indexFaq.a: Upright means the card's theme is coming to the surface; reversed means the theme is excessive, lacking, or turned inward. A reversed card does not mean something “bad” — it is a sign to change how you approach it. Each card's page explains both.
indexFaq.q: How does the meaning change between upright and reversed?

indexFaq.a: Yes, it does. For example, The Tower can be read as the collapse of an assumption when you're thinking about changing jobs, and as a chance to reconsider a relationship when you're thinking about love. Each card's page includes a section, “Reading it for your decision,” with interpretations for different situations.
indexFaq.q: Does the reading change depending on the decision I'm facing, even for the same card?

indexFaq.a: No memorization is needed. The cards are not a tool to predict your future, but questions to help you organize your own thinking. Just reading the keywords of the card you drew and the “questions to ask yourself” can help you notice feelings and conditions you had overlooked.
indexFaq.q: Do I need to memorize the tarot meanings to use them?

indexFaq.a: We recommend starting from the theme closest to what you're torn about right now. The guide by decision brings together, for each of 40 themes such as changing jobs, love, money, and moving house, the cards involved and viewpoints for organizing your thoughts. If you have already drawn a card, please start from that card's page.
indexFaq.q: Which card should I start reading from?

worriesIntro: The bigger the decision, the more likely you are to go around in circles when you think it through alone. Changing jobs, job hunting, a side project, starting your own business, reskilling, how you use money, love, marriage, parting, caregiving, moving house, relationships. None of these has a single right answer, and whichever you choose, you will have to let something go — that is the kind of decision you're torn over.

On this page, for each common decision you're torn over, we bring together “what is making it hard to judge” and “in what order it helps to think it through,” and introduce tarot cards that can lend you a viewpoint in that situation. Please use the cards not to predict your future, but as questions to help you notice feelings and conditions you had overlooked.

On each page, after explaining how to break down what you're torn about from four viewpoints, we explain one by one why each related card is useful in that situation. Start reading from a theme that interests you, and at the end, try laying out your own two options side by side in DECIDE. — you will likely find it easier to see what you truly want to value than when you were only turning it over in your head.

worriesSteps.text: Open the one closest to what you're torn about right now. It doesn't have to be an exact match.
With “What is making this decision hard” and “Viewpoints for organizing your thoughts,” put into words what you are getting stuck on.
Read the meanings of the related cards and look for feelings and conditions you had overlooked.
Picture your two options, and draw a card in DECIDE.
